claim: The record proposes the commercial section (b67, CPCA 531 as replaced by Law 22-13) but never says that the same law replaced CPCA 534 so that the president of the commercial section must first refer every dispute to mediation, without the parties' consent. The checklist asks the question (k55) and nothing in the record answers it.

source.what: Law 22-13 of 12 July 2022 amending CPCA 08-09, art. 3 (new CPCA art. 534), Official Journal no. 48 of 17 July 2022, pp. 3-4

quoteArabic: "المادّة 534 : يجب على رئيس القسم التجاري عرض النزاع مسبقا على الوساطة. لا تخضع الوساطة أمام القسم التجاري إلى قبول الأطراف، خلافا لأحكام المادّة 994 من هذا القانون. تطبّق على الوساطة أمام القسم التجاري أحكام الوساطة المنصوص عليها في هذا القانون".
consequence: Wherever the record sends the claim to the commercial section, it should tell the lawyer that compulsory mediation comes before the hearing. Law 22-13 art. 13 defers only the jurisdiction rules for the administrative and specialised commercial courts, not art. 534. This also matters for timing: the lessee's three months (d1) target the service of the summons, and mediation does not move that date.

claim: Boundary n15 says that the texts 'do not say which court is competent' when the lessor or lessee is the State, a wilaya, a commune or a public administrative body, and the record still proposes the commercial section. CPCA 800 ¶2 does name the court: the administrative court hears every case to which these persons are party. CPCA 802 lists the exceptions, and no lease dispute is among them.

source.what: Law 22-13 of 12 July 2022, art. 4 (new CPCA art. 800), Official Journal no. 48 of 17 July 2022, p. 5; the 2008 wording (store, cpca 800 ¶2, version law-08-09) is the same on this point

quoteArabic: تختص المحاكم الإدارية بالفصل في أول درجة بحكم قابل للاستئناف في جميع القضايا التي تكون الدولة أو الولاية أو البلدية أو إحدى المؤسسات العمومية ذات الصبغة الإدارية أو الهيئات العمومية الوطنية والمنظمات المهنية الوطنية طرفا فيها.
consequence: When public_body_party is yes and the body is the State, a wilaya, a commune or a public administrative body, the record should give an exit to the administrative court (at least a warning that names CPCA 800), not 'court to check' while the commercial section stays proposed. Public economic enterprises (b4, Commercial Code 170 ¶3) are not covered by CPCA 800, so the slot should tell the two apart.

claim: Request r9 ('order renewal of the lease for (...) and fix its rent and terms') is offered for every pre-2005 commercial lease, citing 197 ¶1. But 176 ¶1 lets the lessor refuse renewal, with the eviction compensation as the only sanction, and 197 ¶1 gives the lessee only two actions: contesting the ground of the refusal or claiming the compensation. A court fixes the terms of a renewal only where the lessor accepted it (195), is deemed to have accepted it (174 ¶4), or later chooses renewal under 197 ¶6.

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 of 26 September 1975 (Commercial Code), arts. 176 and 197, Official Journal no. 101 of 19 December 1975, pp. 1323 and 1327

quoteArabic: المادة 176 : يجوز للمؤجر أن يرفض تجديد الايجار، غير أنه ينبغي عليه فيما عدا الاستثناءات المنصوص عليها في المادة 177 وما يليها أن يسدد للمستأجر المخلى التعويض ... / المادة 197 : اذا رفض المؤجر تجديد الايجار ورغب المستأجر اما في منازعة سبب هذا الرفض، أو طلب سداد تعويض الاخلاء ...
consequence: r9 should be offered only where renewal was accepted, deemed accepted (n4) or chosen by the lessor under 197 ¶6. After a refusal, the lessee's request is the compensation (r3), not a judgment ordering the renewal. As written, a lawyer may draft a request the court will reject as having no legal basis.

claim: Request r2 asks, for every pre-2005 lease, that the lessee leave 'once he has received the eviction compensation', and r5 records a right to stay until it is paid. Article 187 ¶1 gives that right only to a lessee who can claim the compensation. It does not reach a refusal on a serious and legitimate ground (177 ¶1, after the warning of 177 ¶2), demolition for unfitness or danger (177 ¶3), a lessee without the operating period of 172, or substitute premises (187 ¶2: he leaves once the provisional compensation is paid).

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 (Commercial Code), arts. 177 and 187, Official Journal no. 101 of 19 December 1975, pp. 1323-1325

quoteArabic: المادة 187 : لا يجوز الزام أى مستأجر يمكنه المطالبة بتعويض الاخلاء بمغادرة الاماكن قبل قبض التعويض / المادة 177 : يجوز للمؤجر أن يرفض تجديد الايجار دون أن يلزم بسداد أى تعويض، اذا برهن عن سبب خطير ومشروع تجاه المستأجر المخلى المحل
consequence: r2 needs a second wording, eviction without compensation on the ground of 177 (or of 172 lacking), conditioned on refusal_without_compensation_for_breach or a demolition slot. r5 should be offered only when compensation is owed. As written, the lessor's own petition concedes a compensation the law may not impose.

claim: The slot that triggers d2 lists the nullity of a notice to quit as an action 'other than contesting a refusal to renew', so a lessee's action to annul the notice gets the two-year limitation of 198 and d1 stays silent. But the Code treats the notice to quit as the lessor's refusal to renew: 175 ¶3 names it as one of the two ways the lessor notifies his refusal, 178 ¶4 joins 'the act refusing renewal or the notice to quit', and 173 ¶5 requires the notice to restate 194, whose three months run from that notification. A lessee attacking the notice is contesting the refusal, which 198 excludes when it carves out the actions of 196 and 197.

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 (Commercial Code), arts. 173 ¶5, 175 ¶3, 194 ¶1, 197 ¶3, 198 ¶1, Official Journal no. 101 of 19 December 1975, pp. 1323, 1326, 1327

quoteArabic: غير انه عندما يبلغ المؤجر عن طريق التنبيه بالاخلاء او عن طريق رفض التجديد عن نيته فى عدم تجديد الايجار ... / ويجب في هذه الحالة تبليغ التكليف بالحضور في الثلاثة أشهر من تاريخ تبليغ رفض التجديد / ترفع جميع الدعاوى الممارسة وفقا لما ورد في هذا الباب ماعدا الدعاوى المشار اليها في المادتين 196 و 197 أعلاه ... ويشملها التقادم بعد مرور سنتين
consequence: Remove the nullity of the notice to quit from the slot's examples, or let d1 also fire (warning) for a lessee's claim that attacks a notice to quit (r4). Otherwise a lessee's lawyer is told he has two years when the protective reading gives him three months from service of the notice.

claim: Prior step p1 and its slot know only one case: notice six months before 'the end of the lease term'. 173 ¶3 and ¶4, in the same article, add two common cases. A lease ending on a resolutory condition ends only by a notification six months ahead that must mention the fulfilment of the condition. A lease in stages (the usual 3-6-9) needs the notice within the periods of ¶1 before the end of the stage at which the lessor ends it.

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 (Commercial Code), art. 173 ¶3 and ¶4, Official Journal no. 101 of 19 December 1975, p. 1323

quoteArabic: لا تنتهي مدة الإيجار الواقف على شرط والذي يسمح تحقيقه للمؤجر بأن يطلب الفسخ إلا بتبليغ واقع قبل ستة أشهر قبل الأجل ولأجل مألوف، ويجب أن يشير هذا الإعلان إلى تحقيق الشرط المنصوص عليه في العقد. وعندما يتضمن الإيجار عدة مراحل فإنه يجب التنبيه بالإخلاء في الآجال المنصوص عليها في الفقرة الأولى أعلاه، إذا فسخ المؤجر الإيجار في نهاية إحدى هذه المراحل.
consequence: The slot question should measure the six months from the end of the stage at which the lease is ended (¶4). For a conditional lease, it should also ask whether the notification mentions the fulfilment of the condition (¶3). Otherwise a lawyer ending a 3-6-9 lease at the third year gets a wrong question, and a conditional-lease notice without the mention passes.

claim: Lead only. A settled line of the Supreme Court (commercial chamber), as commonly reported, reads the three months of 194/197 as a forfeiture period. A lessee served with a valid notice to quit who does not sue within it loses the eviction compensation and becomes an occupant without right or title, whom the lessor may have evicted without compensation. The record keeps the 'directory period' reading on an equal footing (d1 readings, o2), and r2 and r5 always pair the eviction with prior payment of compensation.

source.what: My own memory of Supreme Court decisions published in المجلة القضائية (no decision number or date retrieved). Searches of coursupreme.dz through the web search in this run found nothing; a Bejaia university thesis on the effects of the notice to quit (univ-bejaia.dz handle 123456789/24223) could not be read (text not extractable).

quoteArabic: المستأجر الذي لم يرفع دعواه خلال أجل ثلاثة أشهر من تاريخ تبليغه بالتنبيه بالإخلاء يسقط حقه في التعويض الاستحقاقي ويصبح شاغلا بدون حق ولا سند (wording from memory, not verified)
consequence: If this is verified on the Supreme Court's own publications, the forfeiture reading should be the record's protective lead for the lessee (d1). The lessor side also needs a case: a pre-2005 lessor seeking eviction after the lessee let the three months pass, where r2's 'after receiving the compensation' would be wrong.

claim: The slot for the operating period (two consecutive years, or four) does not say when the period must be complete. 172 ¶4 fixes it: the period ends at the end of the lease or, where the lease was extended, at the date of the notice to quit or at the usual term after the renewal request. Counting up to the petition date, which the question invites, can wrongly satisfy the condition.

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 (Commercial Code), art. 172 ¶4, Official Journal no. 101 of 19 December 1975, p. 1323

quoteArabic: وتنتهى هذه المدة بانتهاء عقد الايجار او عند الاقتضاء بتاريخ تمديده حسبما هو منصوص عليه فى المادة 173 التالية، ويعتبر هذا التاريخ الاخير اما بمثابة التاريخ الذى تم فيه التنبيه باخلاء واما الاجل المألوف الذى يلى هذا الطلب ... فى حالة وقوع طلب تجديد
consequence: The question of n5 should ask whether the two or four years were complete at the end of the lease, or at the date of the notice to quit or of the term after the renewal request, and should cite 172 ¶4.
